text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty alert fired: PD-14567 — High 5xx rate on inference-serving-prod (model=redwood-13b-v2). Trigger: error-rate > 5% for 3m. Primary: @mike, Escalation policy: inference-sre-prod. Link: https://redwood.pagerduty.com/incidents/PD-14567

pagerduty: Page sent to primary (mike) at 2026-03-14T02:12:12Z — waiting for ack. Policy: 2-mines/10-min escalations configured.

mike: ugh saw this on my watch list but on a call, will try to jump in in ~5.

incident-bot: Reminder: PD escalation timer 8m remaining.

(8 minutes pass)

pagerduty: No ack from primary. Escalating to secondary (aj). Manager escalation will fire at 10m if unacked.

aj: ack — jumping on this. grabbing logs + looking at autoscaler. :eyes:

aj: summary so far — error spikes across two fronting pods, 502s from model host. CPU fine, GPU memory creeping up. Likely KV cache thrash after recent rollout.

sara: tagging infra: did we push the redwood-13b-v2 canary yesterday?

kim: yes, 02:00 deploy included quantized kernel tweaks. rollout was canary 10% then 100% this morning. No obvious alerts until now.

aj: running quick grep on logs:
```
# tail -n 200 /var/log/inference/prod.log | grep "KV cache miss" | wc -l
1200
```

aj: looks like a sudden increase in KV cache misses correlated with request latency spikes. Might be bug in new kernel's cache eviction.

ops-manager: if this is rollout-related, consider immediate rollback of the runtime patch. Who can perform?

mike: (in channel) just woke up — apologies. if aj's got it, i'll stand down for now. if you want me to roll back i can also.

aj: i'll attempt a quick rollback on a single node to validate. prepping command.

deploy-bot: deploy rollback started: reverting runtime image redwood/runtime:2026-03-14-kernel-fix -> redwood/runtime:2026-03-13-stable on node p-13a.

aj: monitoring metrics... err rate dropping on node p-13a within 40s. good sign. rolling back remaining nodes in 3m unless regressions.

incident-bot: PagerDuty note — secondary (aj) acknowledged at 2026-03-14T02:22:10Z. Manager escalation canceled.

aj: rolling remaining nodes back now. passing health checks.

mike: thanks aj. I'll follow up with the quant/kernels owners in the morning. can we confirm customer impact?

aj: quick impact check: about 8% of production requests saw 5xx during the 14 minute window. Affected tenants: two mid-market customers reported increased latency, no data loss. We posted a status notice draft to #status-downtime.

ops-manager: good initial mitigation. please add a short customer-facing summary for support and CS: what happened, which models affected, timeframe, mitigation steps, and whether they'll need to resubmit requests.

aj: draft for support: "From 02:12–02:26 UTC a runtime kernel rollout caused increased KV cache misses leading to elevated 5xx responses for the redwood-13b-v2 model. We rolled back the runtime and error rates returned to baseline. No data loss; transient failures may have affected some requests — retry recommended. Engineers are investigating root cause and will follow up."

kim: forwarding to model infra and quant team. we'll snapshot kernels and run bisect today.

mike: adding follow-up tasks: 1) bisect kernel change, 2) improve canary criteria to catch KV miss regressions, 3) add alert for KV miss rate. I'll own #2.

aj: closing loop here — incident mitigation complete, error rate stable for 10+ mins. recommend we close PD incident once post-mortem ticket created.

incident-bot: PD-14567 updated: Status -> Mitigated. Escalation history: primary no ack -> secondary ack -> rollback mitigated.

ops-manager: great work. please ensure the postmortem includes timeline, missed primary ack note (mike was on-call but didn't ack due to meeting), and any PD escalation tuning suggestions.

mike: noted -- i'll add my timeline and why I missed the first page (on-call overlap with all-hands). will propose paging schedule tweak. :hourglass_flowing_sand:

aj: launching a short blameless postmortem doc now and assigning to eng-ml + eng-runtime.

sara: adding a follow-up to improve incident-bot message verbosity so it's clearer who is currently expected to ack. small UX fix may reduce missed acks.

incident-bot: thread closed for now. If error rate rises above threshold or PD reopens, re-activate thread. :thumbsup:
